goals.title: Peptides for hair loss vs proven options | Peptide Chooser
goals.h1: Peptides for hair loss, compared with the proven options.
goals.description: Peptides for hair loss next to finasteride and minoxidil: FDA status, evidence in people and price per month for each option, checked and dated.
goals.short_answer: Finasteride and minoxidil are the only treatments on this page the FDA has approved for hair loss, and generic finasteride starts at about $10 a month. Copper peptide serums are cosmetics: the evidence is from lab and follicle-culture studies, not from large trials in people. Injectable peptides sold for hair are not approved for any use, and we found no human evidence for hair.

options.name: Finasteride 1 mg and minoxidil
options.kind: Prescription pill (men) and over-the-counter liquid or foam
options.price_note: generic finasteride with a pharmacy coupon; average cash price $45.80
options.how: Prescription for finasteride; minoxidil over the counter
options.does: Finasteride 1 mg: A daily pill. Slows hair loss and regrows some hair in most men; not for women who may become pregnant. Minoxidil: A liquid or foam you put on the scalp twice a day. Regrows hair for men and women; works while you keep using it.
options.how_plain: Finasteride 1 mg: Prescription, from an online clinic or your doctor. Minoxidil: No prescription, any pharmacy.

options.kind: Sold as cosmetics for the scalp
options.does: A cosmetic serum for the scalp. Small lab and follicle studies; no large trials in people.
options.status_plain: Cosmetic: legal to sell, nobody checked that it works.

options.price_note: We do not list prices or sellers for products that are not approved for human use
options.does: Vials from research-use shops, meant to be injected. No human evidence for hair.

goals.name: Skin
goals.label: Skin
goals.intro: Peptide creams and serums are cosmetics: legal to sell without approval, and judged on their own studies, which are small. The proven prescription option for wrinkles is tretinoin.

peptides.name: Tretinoin cream
peptides.does: A nightly prescription cream. Reduces fine wrinkles and evens skin over months; can irritate at first.

peptides.name: GHK-Cu copper peptide
peptides.does: A serum or cream. Small studies suggest firmer-looking skin; no large trials.

peptides.name: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Matrixyl)
peptides.does: The most common "anti-wrinkle peptide" in creams. Modest effect in small studies.

peptides.name: Acetyl hexapeptide-8 (Argireline)
peptides.does: Sold as "Botox in a bottle"; barely gets through the skin.

goals.for: For fine lines, loss of firmness and dull skin: what a prescription cream does, and what a peptide serum can and cannot do.

goals.name: Weight loss
goals.label: Weight loss
goals.intro: Two peptide drugs are FDA approved for weight management and need a prescription. Compounded copies and newer molecules sold online are not approved.

peptides.name: Semaglutide (Wegovy)
peptides.does: A weekly shot that cuts appetite; about 15 % body weight lost on average in trials.
peptides.how: Prescription; online clinics prescribe after a visit.

peptides.name: Tirzepatide (Zepbound)
peptides.does: A weekly shot, same idea, larger average loss in trials.

peptides.name: Compounded semaglutide or tirzepatide
peptides.does: Pharmacy-made copies sold by online clinics, often cheaper. Not checked by the FDA batch by batch.

peptides.name: Retatrutide
peptides.does: A newer three-hormone shot, still in trials. Sold online only from research-use shops.
peptides.how: We do not link to them.

goals.for: For losing weight with medical help: the two approved weekly shots, what they cost, and the copies sold online.

goals.name: Muscle and hormones
goals.label: Muscle growth
goals.intro: No peptide is FDA approved for building muscle. Tesamorelin is approved for one specific use in people with HIV; growth hormone peptides sold for muscle are not approved.

peptides.name: Tesamorelin (Egrifta)
peptides.does: A daily shot approved only to reduce belly fat in people with HIV. Sold off-label by clinics for "growth hormone".
peptides.status_plain: FDA approved for HIV-related belly fat only.
peptides.top_pick_why: Approved only for HIV-related belly fat, not for muscle (owner, 31 Oct 2026).

peptides.name: Sermorelin
peptides.status: No FDA-approved product on the market
peptides.does: A growth-hormone-releasing shot from compounding pharmacies; the approved brand was taken off the market years ago.
peptides.status_plain: No FDA-approved product on the market.

peptides.name: CJC-1295 / ipamorelin
peptides.does: Growth-hormone-releasing peptides sold by research-use shops and some clinics. No approved product, no large human trials.
peptides.how: We do not link to shops.

goals.for: For building muscle or "boosting growth hormone": no peptide is approved for that. Here is what the sold ones actually are.

goals.name: Recovery and joints
goals.label: Healing and joints
goals.intro: Nothing is approved for injury recovery. In July 2026 an FDA advisory committee reviewed BPC-157 and TB-500 for pharmacy compounding, and the FDA proposed keeping both off the list.

peptides.name: BPC-157
peptides.status: Not approved; FDA proposed excluding it from compounding (Jul 2026)
peptides.does: The most searched "healing peptide". Animal studies only; the FDA reviewed it for pharmacy compounding on 23 Jul 2026 and proposed keeping it off the list.

peptides.name: TB-500
peptides.status: Not approved; FDA proposed excluding it from compounding (Jul 2026)
peptides.does: A copy of a natural repair protein, sold alongside BPC-157. Same July 2026 review, same proposal.

goals.for: For tendon, joint and injury healing: the peptides people inject for this, and why none is approved.

goals.name: Sexual health
goals.label: Sex drive
goals.intro: One peptide is FDA approved, for low sexual desire in premenopausal women, and needs a prescription. The same molecule sold as PT-141 by online shops is not an approved product.

peptides.name: Bremelanotide (Vyleesi)
peptides.does: A shot you take before sex, approved for low sexual desire in premenopausal women.

peptides.name: PT-141 from online shops
peptides.does: The same molecule as Vyleesi, sold without a prescription by research-use shops: no dose control, no checks.
peptides.how: We do not link to them.

peptides.name: Melanotan II
peptides.does: A tanning peptide also sold "for libido". Linked to serious side effects; never approved anywhere.
peptides.how: We do not link to them.

goals.for: For low desire or arousal: one approved option for women, and what the online "PT-141" really is.

goals.name: Longevity and energy
goals.label: Energy and aging
goals.intro: No peptide is approved for aging or energy. The ones sold for it were reviewed by an FDA advisory committee in July 2026, and the FDA proposed keeping them off the compounding list.

peptides.name: Epitalon
peptides.status: Not approved; FDA proposed excluding it from compounding (Jul 2026)
peptides.does: A four-amino-acid peptide sold as an "anti-aging" shot; human evidence is thin and old. Reviewed by the FDA in July 2026; proposed exclusion.

peptides.name: MOTS-c
peptides.status: Not approved; FDA proposed excluding it from compounding (Jul 2026)
peptides.does: A "mitochondrial" peptide sold for energy; animal studies only. Same July 2026 review.

peptides.name: NAD+ injections
peptides.status: Not a peptide; compounded, not FDA approved
peptides.does: Not a peptide: a vitamin-B3-derived molecule sold by clinics as shots or drips for energy.

goals.for: For "anti-aging" and more energy: what is sold, what the evidence says, and what is not even a peptide.

glossary.text: the FDA checked that it works and is safe for this use, and every batch is inspected. Prescription unless marked otherwise.
legal to sell without approval; nobody has to prove it works. Fine on your skin, no claims beyond looks.
a licensed pharmacy mixes it for you on prescription. Legal in limited cases; no batch testing by the FDA.
no approved product exists. Shops sell it "for research". Buying it is not a crime for you, but nobody has checked what is in the vial. We never link to these shops.
only approved products have safety data from large trials. For everything else the honest answer is: unknown.
